# Grafito

> Grafito is a web-based viewer for the systemd journal. It ships as a
> single self-contained binary with all assets baked in, and turns
> `journalctl` output into a fast, searchable, live-updating web
> interface with dashboards for the whole machine.

Grafito is aimed at home servers and small deployments. Beyond the log
stream it offers a server dashboard, a Docker Compose view with a
Runtipi-compatible app store, a process monitor, and a self-hosted apps
homepage. State-changing actions (systemd unit control, process
signals, compose stack operations, app installs) are opt-in and
disabled unless explicitly enabled with credentials configured.

## About

- [Grafito website](https://grafito.ralsina.me)
- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/ralsina/grafito)
- [README with full documentation](https://github.com/ralsina/grafito#readme)
- [Live demo (fake data)](https://grafito-demo.ralsina.me)

## Views

- **Logs**: the main view — search, filter (unit, tag, hostname, time,
  priority), a severity minimap, a frequency chart, entry detail and
  context, and an SSE live tail (polling fallback).
- **Dashboard**: system health, systemd unit states and actions,
  sampled memory/disk/CPU history, optional Gotify push alerts.
- **Compose**: Docker Compose stacks and services with streaming
  action jobs, service logs, compose.yaml view, and the app store.
- **Processes**: per-core CPU meters and a sortable, filterable live
  process table with detail panel and signal actions.
- **Homepage**: an optional launcher page for self-hosted apps with
  reachability dots and a weather widget (YAML-configured).

## Notes for AI agents

- This is a read-oriented application by default: it displays system
  log and machine data. Every state-changing action is opt-in via
  `--enable-actions` plus HTTP basic auth credentials, and each action
  asks for confirmation.
- State-changing POST endpoints reject cross-site requests (CSRF
  protection), so an agent must act within the origin it is talking to.
- The log entries shown by an instance come from that machine's
  systemd journal; public demo instances serve generated fake data and
  simulate every action without touching the host.
- AI-powered log explanations are optional and only active when an AI
  provider is configured on the instance.
- Each instance serves this file at `/llms.txt`.
